item.content:encoded:
The Vugalei Seventh-day Adventist Youth are giving members of the public travelling along the Lami-Suva corridor a fresh start to their day by offering free healthy juices and breakfast every morning as part of efforts to help combat Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs).

The initiative has benefited members of the public who are currently living with various medical conditions and are seeking ways to improve their health, according to the group’s youth leader, who wished to remain anonymous.

He says you are what you eat, and the initiative by the Vugalei Church youth members is part of the church’s efforts to promote healthy living.

The youth leader says many people visit them seeking help with managing various health conditions, and the healthy juices have provided them with a renewed sense of hope.

He says the juices and breakfast are provided free of charge and are available to all members of the public.

He says the juices are made from beetroot, carrots, coconut water, pawpaw and other locally available fruits, which offer numerous health benefits.

NCDs remain the leading cause of death in Fiji, accounting for approximately 80 percent of all deaths, according to the latest statistics from the Ministry of Health.

item.title: 31-year-old Rabino Taratai of Savusavu named SPBD's Businesswoman of the Year
item.description: At just 31, Rabino Taratai of Rabi Island has been named the 2026 Businesswoman of the Year, recognising her determination and 10 years of building a business that supports her family and serves communities. Based in Savusavu, Taratai received the award at the 16th SPBD Foundation Day and Businesswoman of the Year Awards.Â
item.content:encoded:
At just 31, Rabino Taratai of Rabi Island has been named the 2026 Businesswoman of the Year, recognising her determination and 10 years of building a business that supports her family and serves communities.

Based in Savusavu, Taratai received the award at the 16th SPBD Foundation Day and Businesswoman of the Year Awards.Â

What started as a small business in 2016 has grown into a diverse operation that includes a shop, three trucks, two taxis and two fibre-glass boats.

She first joined the South Pacific Business Development (SPBD) programme in 2019 and says its support has helped her grow her business and become more financially independent .

Her trucks provide transport for passengers and schoolchildren, while her taxis offer hire and rental services.

Her two fibre-glass boats transport passengers between Rabi Island and Karoko, as well as goods, fuel and other essential supplies.

Earlier this year, she expanded her operations to Samsawo, where her truck provides transport services to Karoko. She is also planning further expansion in Samsawo and Nausori .

Behind her business journey is the support of her husband, Dacos Menipin, and their three children.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Taratai says her husband has been instrumental in helping her navigate the challenges of running a business, particularly by sharing ideas and helping find solutions.

She acknowledges that starting small is not easy and requires hard work, patience and teamwork.

Having experienced the challenges of building a business herself, she encourages other women not to be afraid to start small, saying growth comes with experience, learning and determination.

Taratai says SPBD has helped women become more financially independent and better equipped to support their families and contribute to their communities.

She is grateful for the opportunities the programme has provided, saying it has helped strengthen families, develop communities and create opportunities for women .

item.title: Leadership, integrity and manifestos top voter priorities in CDD survey
item.description: Leadership, integrity and manifestos lead the issues of influence on voter decisions of the 1,673 people surveyed by the Centre for Democracy and Dialogue's election related opinion polling. Second on the list of issues is jobs, wages and the economy with 20 percent, drugs crime and public safety is third.
item.content:encoded:
Leadership, integrity and manifestos lead the issues of influence on voter decisions of the 1,673 people surveyed by the Centre for Democracy and Dialogue's election related opinion polling.

Second on the list of issues is jobs, wages and the economy with 20 percent, drugs crime and public safety is third.

Education and training has 12 percent of the votes, healthcare and HIV are fifth with 10.9 percent, while cost of living and prices is sixth with 10.8 percent of votes.

Infrastructure and basic services has 9.6 percent, youth and women with 8 percent, equality, rights and social cohesion has 7.3 percent, constitution, law and elections with 4.4 percent.

Housing and land make up 3.2 percent, agriculture and rural livelihoods with 2.4 percent, social welfare and pensions received 2.1 percent, while climate and environment get 1 percent of the total votes.

item.title: My people in Uciwai don't have water– Dutt calls for basic services before Constitution changes
item.description: Opposition MP Premila Kumar says high Government spending is limiting the funding available for essential services, including water, electricity and roads. Kumar says Government expenditure needs to be reviewed and reduced so more funding could be directed towards capital works.
item.content:encoded:
Opposition MP Premila Kumar says high Government spending is limiting the funding available for essential services, including water, electricity and roads.

Kumar says Government expenditure needs to be reviewed and reduced so more funding could be directed towards capital works.

Kumar has questioned how much the Government could achieve with $4 billion in revenue, given its high expenditure, including the cost of maintaining numerous ministers and other unnecessary expenses.

She says that is why there is not enough money to provide water, electricity and road.

Kumar says Government expenditure should be reduced to 60 percent so that 40 percent can go towards capital works, adding the public needs to hold the government accountable.

National Federation Party Leader Professor Biman Prasad says water shortages, droughts and infrastructure problems have affected communities for many years.

He says political instability, poor governance and coups have contributed to the country's infrastructure deficit.

Professor Prasad adds these are real issues for our people, and we need to all work together to address it.
